title: FAMU vs TSU: tuition, size, location
summary: Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University (FAMU) versus Tennessee State University (TSU). Also searched as TSU vs FAMU. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Tennessee State University vs Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University (TSU vs FAMU) are both public institutions but differ in several key aspects. TSU, located in Nashville, has an undergraduate enrollment of 4,848 students, whereas FAMU in Tallahassee enrolls 7,582 undergraduates. Tuition for in-state students at TSU is $8,616, which is higher compared to FAMU's $5,785. These differences highlight variations in size, location, and cost between the two universities.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing Tennessee State University vs Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University (TSU vs FAMU) in terms of cost, there are notable differences. TSU's tuition for in-state students is $8,616, while FAMU charges $5,785 for in-state tuition. For out-of-state students, TSU's tuition is $22,416, which is higher than FAMU's $17,725. Additionally, the median debt for students who complete their degrees at TSU is $27,000, compared to $23,548 at FAMU. These figures indicate that TSU generally has higher tuition and median student debt than FAMU.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: Tennessee State University vs Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University (TSU vs FAMU) both offer traditional campus-based learning models in their respective cities. TSU is situated in Nashville, Tennessee, serving an undergraduate population of 4,848 students. In contrast, FAMU is located in Tallahassee, Florida, with a larger undergraduate enrollment of 7,582 students. Both universities provide in-person educational experiences that support their student bodies within urban settings.

sections.heading: Pick FAMU if
paragraphs: Pick Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University vs Tennessee State University (FAMU vs TSU) if you seek a public university with a more selective admission rate, as FAMU admits about 20.56% of applicants.
